newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan firm to withdraw from stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan firm to withdraw from stock exchange.

text.p: Morocco's portfolio company Societe Epargne Croissance said on Monday it would be delisted from the Casablanca stock exchange on August 6 because its shares were not being traded enough.
A company spokesman said: "We asked the bourse watchdog CDVM to delist us because with only one percent of our capital listed, it was not regularly traded."
Al-Amane insurance holds 99 percent of the company which last traded in May.
The bourse regulatory body, Conseil Deontologique des Valeurs Mobilieres (CDVM) which was set up in 1994 to regulate trade on the stock exchange, has delisted 18 companies since then.
There are 48 companies listed on the Casablanca bourse.
